Why split. The supplied proof bundles five independent heavy obligations of Simon Ch. 6, plus support bookkeeping:
- the current defined by the formula 2.24(2) (steps 2(a)–(b));
- the representation-independent extension by smooth approximation (2(c), 3(b));
- the mass estimate from Cauchy–Binet and Hadamard (1(a), 5);
- preservation of cycles (step 7, 2.24(1));
- integrality by the area formula (step 6, 3.3–3.9);
- the support facts (1(b)–(c), 3(a), 4).
The pinned SimonGMT has only the affine push-forward. Two of these obligations are already comparator-accepted for C¹ maps φ that equal the identity off a compact set: dpf_pushforward_formula_current_exists (the integral is a current) and dpf_pushforward_formula_boundaryVanishes (cycles go to cycles). subproblems.title: A C¹ map near a compact set agrees there with a compactly supported C¹ perturbation of the identity (the cut-off of Simon 6.2.23)
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, O ⊆ ℝ^P open, K ⊆ O compact, and f : ℝ^P → ℝ^P of class C¹ on O (ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f O). Then there exist a map φ : ℝ^P → ℝ^P of class C¹ on all of ℝ^P (ContDiff ℝ 1 φ), an open set V ⊆ ℝ^P with K ⊆ V, and a compact set K' ⊆ ℝ^P such that φ(x) = f(x) and Dφ(x) = Df(x) for every x ∈ V (Df(x) := fderiv ℝ f x), and φ(x) = x for every x ∉ K'.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (O K : Set (Euclid P)) (f : Euclid P → Euclid P), IsOpen O → IsCompact K → K ⊆ O → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f O → ∃ (φ : Euclid P → Euclid P) (V K' : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen V ∧ K ⊆ V ∧ IsCompact K' ∧ ContDiff ℝ 1 φ ∧ (∀ x ∈ V, φ x = f x ∧ fderiv ℝ φ x = fderiv ℝ f x) ∧ ∀ x, x ∉ K' → φ x = x
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the cut-off χ ∈ C_c^∞(O) with χ = 1 on a neighbourhood of K (resp. of closure(V)) in steps 2(c) and 7(a) of the parent proof, i.e. the function ζ of Simon Ch. 6, 2.23 (chapter-06.txt lines 404–413: ζ ∈ C_c^∞(U) identically equal to one in a neighbourhood of a compact set). Here the cut-off is applied to f − id, so that the parent's steps 2(a)–(b) (the integral defines a current) and 7 (∂ of the push-forward of a cycle vanishes) can be carried out for a globally C¹ map φ that equals the identity off a compact set and coincides with f, to first order, near K.
Notation: E := ℝ^P (a proper space); for δ > 0, thickening(δ, K) := {x : infEdist(x, K) < δ} (open) and cthickening(δ, K) := {x : infEdist(x, K) ≤ δ} (closed).
1. Margin. Since K is compact, O is open and K ⊆ O, there is ρ > 0 with cthickening(ρ, K) ⊆ O (Mathlib IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). Put δ := ρ/2 > 0, so cthickening(2δ, K) ⊆ O. (If K = ∅ all thickenings below are empty and the construction still works.)
2. Smooth cut-off. Let s := thickening(2δ, K), an open set, and t := cthickening(δ, K), a closed set; t ⊆ s because infEdist(x, K) ≤ δ < 2δ. By the smooth Urysohn lemma for finite-dimensional real normed spaces (Mathlib exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff, applied to the open s and the closed t ⊆ s) there is χ : E → ℝ of class C^∞ with values in [0, 1], support χ = s and χ(x) = 1 for every x ∈ t. Put K' := tsupport χ = closure(s). Then K' ⊆ cthickening(2δ, K) (closure of a thickening lies in the closed thickening) ⊆ O, and K' is compact, being a closed subset of the compact set cthickening(2δ, K) (IsCompact.cthickening; E is proper). Put V := thickening(δ, K): V is open, K ⊆ V because δ > 0, and V ⊆ t, so χ = 1 on V.
3. Definition. φ(x) := x + χ(x)·(f(x) − x) for every x ∈ E.
4. φ is of class C¹ on E. It suffices to prove ContDiffAt ℝ 1 φ x for every x ∈ E (contDiff_iff_contDiffAt). Since K' ⊆ O, every x lies in O or in E ∖ K'.
 (a) Let x ∈ O. O is an open neighbourhood of x and f is C¹ on O, hence f is C¹ at x (ContDiffOn.contDiffAt, O ∈ 𝓝 x). The identity and χ are C^∞, and sums, differences and products of a scalar C¹ function with a vector-valued C¹ map are C¹ at x (ContDiffAt.add, ContDiffAt.sub, ContDiffAt.smul). So φ = id + χ·(f − id) is C¹ at x.
 (b) Let x ∈ E ∖ K'. This set is open and χ vanishes on it (χ = 0 outside tsupport χ). Hence φ(y) = y for all y in a neighbourhood of x, i.e. φ =ᶠ[𝓝 x] id, and φ is C¹ at x because the identity is (ContDiffAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq).
5. Agreement with f on V. For y ∈ V, χ(y) = 1 and φ(y) = y + (f(y) − y) = f(y). Let x ∈ V. Since V is open, φ and f agree on a neighbourhood of x, i.e. φ =ᶠ[𝓝 x] f; therefore φ(x) = f(x) and Dφ(x) = Df(x) (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq; fderiv at x depends only on the germ at x, also when f is not differentiable there).
6. Identity off K'. If x ∉ K' = tsupport χ then χ(x) = 0, so φ(x) = x.
7. By steps 2–6, φ, V and K' have all the required properties: V is open with K ⊆ V, K' is compact, φ is C¹ on E, φ = f and Dφ = Df on V, and φ = id off K'. ∎
proof_key_steps: Choose δ > 0 with cthickening(2δ, K) ⊆ O and a C^∞ function χ : ℝ^P → [0, 1] with χ = 1 on V := thickening(δ, K) ⊇ K and compact K' := tsupport χ ⊆ O (smooth Urysohn lemma).
Define φ := id + χ·(f − id); it is C¹ at points of O because f is C¹ there, and equals the identity near points outside tsupport χ; these two open sets cover ℝ^P.
On the open set V, φ = f, so φ(x) = f(x) and Dφ(x) = Df(x) for x ∈ V; off K', χ = 0 and φ = id.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse: this is the comparator-accepted DAG declaration dpf_pushforward_formula_current_exists (node root.minimizing_implies_stationary-a1.diffeo_pushforward-a1.pushforward_current-a1, accepted candidate commit 3de784c), whose frozen Lean type is reused verbatim; no new formal work is needed. The parent applies it with U = ℝ^P, R a chosen representation of Y, and the compact set K' and C¹ map φ of the sibling c1_perturbation (built for K = spt Y); this carries out steps 2(a)–(b) of the parent proof (the integral is a current). Its audited proof is reproduced below; in that text, "the parent proof" and "sibling" refer to the decomposition of root.minimizing_implies_stationary-a1.diffeo_pushforward-a1, in which it was proved, not to the present node.
Source: step 2 of the parent proof; Simon 6.2.23–2.24(2)–(3) (chapter-06.txt lines 403–440: f_#T(ω) = ∫⟨ω(f(x)), df_x#ξ(x)⟩θ dH^n, which makes sense for C¹ f with f|spt T proper), with the details filled in. Notation: E := ℝ^P; μ := H^n⌞M = μHE[n].restrict M; for an n-covector β and L ∈ End(E), β∘L := β.compContinuousLinearMap L, so (β∘L)(v₁, …, v_n) = β(Lv₁, …, Lv_n); ‖·‖ denotes operator norms; for ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) put g_ω(x) := θ(x) ξ(x)(ω(φ(x))∘Dφ(x)).
1. Bound on Dφ. K is compact, hence closed, and φ = id on the open set E ∖ K, so Dφ(x) = I for x ∉ K (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq). Dφ is continuous (φ is C¹, ContDiff.continuous_fderiv), hence ‖Dφ‖ ≤ c on K for some c ≥ 0 (IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn). So with Λ := max(1, c), ‖Dφ(x)‖ ≤ Λ for every x ∈ E.
2. Pointwise bounds. By R.orients, for μ-a.e. x there are a subspace Q, an orthonormal τ : Fin n → E and a sign with ξ(x)(β) = ±β(τ) for all n-covectors β; since |β(τ)| ≤ ‖β‖ ∏ᵢ|τᵢ| = ‖β‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm), |ξ(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖ for all β, for μ-a.e. x. Moreover ‖β∘L‖ ≤ ‖β‖ ‖L‖^n (ContinuousAlternatingMap.norm_compContinuousLinearMap_le). (For n = 0, τ is empty, β(τ) is the value of the 0-covector β, and β∘L = β.)
3. Support of g_ω. Let ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U); tsupport ω is compact and contained in U, so C_ω := tsupport ω ∪ K is a compact subset of U. If g_ω(x) ≠ 0 then ω(φ(x)) ≠ 0, so φ(x) ∈ tsupport ω; if moreover x ∉ K then x = φ(x) ∈ tsupport ω. Hence g_ω(x) ≠ 0 implies φ(x) ∈ tsupport ω and x ∈ C_ω.
4. Integrability. g_ω is μ-a.e. strongly measurable: x ↦ θ(x) is measurable (R.measurable_mult, ℕ-valued), ξ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (R.aestronglyMeasurable_orient), x ↦ ω(φ(x))∘Dφ(x) is continuous (ω is smooth hence continuous, φ and Dφ are continuous, and (β, L) ↦ β∘L = compContinuousLinearMapCLM L β is jointly continuous: ContinuousAlternatingMap.continuous_compContinuousLinearMapCLM together with joint continuity of the evaluation of continuous linear maps), and the evaluation (ξ, β) ↦ ξ(β) is a continuous bilinear map. By steps 1–3, for μ-a.e. x: |g_ω(x)| ≤ Λ^n ‖ω‖_∞ θ(x) 1_{C_ω}(x), where ‖ω‖_∞ := sup_y ‖ω(y)‖ < ∞ (ω is continuous with compact support). By R.locallyIntegrable_mult, ∫⁻_{M∩C_ω} θ dH^n < ∞ (∫⁻_M θ 1_{C_ω} dH^n = ∫⁻_{M∩C_ω} θ dH^n by lintegral_indicator and Measure.restrict_restrict, C_ω being closed), so the bound is μ-integrable and g_ω ∈ L¹(μ).
5. Linearity. For fixed x, ω ↦ g_ω(x) is linear: (ω₁ + cω₂)(φ(x))∘Dφ(x) = ω₁(φ(x))∘Dφ(x) + c ω₂(φ(x))∘Dφ(x) (compContinuousLinearMap is linear in the covector) and ξ(x) is linear. Since every g_ω is integrable (step 4), S₀(ω) := ∫ g_ω dμ is an ℝ-linear map 𝒟^n(U) → ℝ (integral_add, integral_smul).
6. Sequential continuity. Let (ω_j) be a sequence in 𝒟^n(U) with TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0: there is a compact C ⊆ U containing tsupport ω_j for all j, and (the case k = 0 of the definition; ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 f x‖ = ‖f x‖, norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero) ε_j := sup_{y∈C} ‖ω_j(y)‖ → 0. For μ-a.e. x, step 3 gives g_{ω_j}(x) = 0 unless φ(x) ∈ C and x ∈ C ∪ K, so |g_{ω_j}(x)| ≤ Λ^n ε_j θ(x) 1_{C∪K}(x). Hence |S₀(ω_j)| ≤ Λ^n ε_j ∫_{M∩(C∪K)} θ dH^n → 0, the last integral being finite by R.locallyIntegrable_mult (C ∪ K is a compact subset of U).
7. Conclusion. S := ⟨S₀, step 6⟩ is a GeometricCurrentOn U n, and S(ω) = S₀(ω) = ∫_M θ(x) ξ(x)(ω(φ(x))∘Dφ(x)) dH^n(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) by definition. (Neither openness of U nor bijectivity of φ was used.)
proof_key_steps: Dφ = I off K and is continuous, so ‖Dφ‖ ≤ Λ on E.
|ξ(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖ a.e. on M from the unit orientation, and ‖β∘L‖ ≤ ‖β‖‖L‖^n.
g_ω vanishes unless φ(x) ∈ tsupport ω, hence off the compact set tsupport ω ∪ K ⊆ U.
g_ω is a.e. strongly measurable and dominated by Λ^n‖ω‖_∞ θ 1_{C_ω}, integrable by local integrability of θ.
S₀(ω) := ∫ g_ω is linear, and |S₀(ω_j)| ≤ Λ^n sup‖ω_j‖ ∫_{M∩(C∪K)} θ → 0 gives sequential continuity.

Source: step 3 of the parent proof; Simon 6.2.24(1) (chapter-06.txt line 414: ∂f_#T = f_#∂T), extended from smooth f to C¹ f through 2.24(2) (lines 415–425) by approximating φ with smooth maps; details filled in. Notation: E := ℝ^P; μ := H^n⌞M; for a smooth map χ : E → E and a form α of degree d, χ^#α(x) := α(χ(x))∘Dχ(x) (= SimonGMT pullbackFormWithin univ χ α, since fderivWithin on univ is fderiv, fderivWithin_univ); d := exteriorDerivative = extDeriv.
1. Reduction. If n = 0, BoundaryVanishes S is True by definition. Let n = m + 1 and assume T.boundary = 0. By extensionality of currents (GeometricCurrentOn.ext) it suffices to prove S.boundary(η) = 0 for every η ∈ 𝒟^m(U). By GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply, S.boundary(η) = S(exteriorDerivativeTestOn U m η), the test form whose underlying form is dη. Fix η ∈ 𝒟^m(U).

Naturality of d. d(ψ_k^#η) = ψ_k^#(dη) as forms on E: this is SimonGMT exteriorDerivativeOn_pullbackFormWithin with domains univ (open), ψ_k C^∞ on univ, MapsTo univ univ and η smooth (it rests on Mathlib extDerivWithin_pullback), together with the identifications exteriorDerivativeOn univ α = extDerivWithin α univ = extDeriv α = dα (Mathlib extDerivWithin_univ) and pullbackFormWithin univ ψ_k α = ψ_k^#α (Mathlib fderivWithin_univ). If h_k(x) ≠ 0 then ψ_k(x) ∈ tsupport(dη) ⊆ tsupport η, and if moreover x ∉ K' then x = ψ_k(x); so h_k(x) ≠ 0 implies x ∈ C₀ := tsupport η ∪ K', a compact subset of U. Lemma S (smooth approximation of a compactly supported C¹ perturbation of the identity). Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, K ⊆ U compact and φ : ℝ^P → ℝ^P a C¹ map with φ(x) = x for x ∉ K. Then there are C^∞ maps ψ_k : ℝ^P → ℝ^P (k ∈ ℕ), a compact K' ⊆ U and a constant C such that ψ_k(x) = x for x ∉ K' and all k, ‖Dψ_k(x)‖ ≤ C for all k and x, and ψ_k(x) → φ(x), Dψ_k(x) → Dφ(x) as k → ∞ for every x.
Proof of Lemma S. Source: the mollification φ_k := id + ρ_k ∗ (φ − id) in step 3 of the parent proof (used to reduce Simon 6.2.24(1), chapter-06.txt line 414, ∂f_#T = f_#∂T, from C¹ maps to smooth maps), with the details filled in. Notation: E := ℝ^P, I := identity, λ := Lebesgue measure (volume) on E, ∗ convolution with respect to λ; in Lean ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) is the C^∞ condition (the coercion of ⊤ : ℕ∞ to WithTop ℕ∞, not the analytic order).
1. Margin. Since K is compact, U open and K ⊆ U, there is δ > 0 with K' := cthickening δ K = {x : infEdist(x, K) ≤ δ} ⊆ U (Mathlib IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open; if K = ∅ then K' = ∅). K' is compact (IsCompact.cthickening, E proper).
2. The perturbation. g := φ − id : E → E is C¹, and g(x) = 0 for x ∉ K; so g and Dg = Dφ − I (Dg = 0 on the open set E ∖ K by Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq) are continuous with support in the compact set K. Hence g has compact support, and A := sup_x ‖Dg(x)‖ < ∞.
3. Mollifiers. For k ∈ ℕ let β_k : ContDiffBump (0 : E) have 0 < rIn < rOut = δ/(k+2), and ρ_k := β_k.normed λ: ρ_k is C^∞, ρ_k ≥ 0 (ContDiffBump.nonneg_normed), ∫ ρ_k dλ = 1 (ContDiffBump.integral_normed) and ρ_k(y) = 0 for |y| ≥ δ/(k+2) (its support is the open ball of radius rOut). Define ψ_k := id + ρ_k ∗ g, i.e. ψ_k(x) = x + ∫ ρ_k(t) g(x − t) dt (the convolution ρ_k ⋆[lsmul ℝ ℝ, λ] g).
4. Smoothness. ρ_k is C^∞ with compact support and g is continuous, hence locally integrable, so ρ_k ∗ g is C^∞ (Mathlib HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left with n = ⊤ : ℕ∞; λ is invariant under translations and negation). Hence ψ_k is C^∞.
5. Support. Let x ∉ K'. For every t with ρ_k(t) ≠ 0 we have |t| < δ/(k+2) < δ, and x − t ∉ K (otherwise infEdist(x, K) ≤ |t| < δ, i.e. x ∈ K'). So g(x − t) = 0 whenever ρ_k(t) ≠ 0, (ρ_k ∗ g)(x) = 0 and ψ_k(x) = x, for every k.
6. Derivative bound. g is C¹ with compact support and ρ_k is locally integrable, so ρ_k ∗ g is differentiable with D(ρ_k ∗ g)(x) = (ρ_k ⋆[(lsmul ℝ ℝ).precompR E, λ] Dg)(x) = ∫ ρ_k(t) Dg(x − t) dt (Mathlib HasCompactSupport.hasFDerivAt_convolution_right, the derivative falling on the compactly supported C¹ factor g). Therefore Dψ_k(x) = I + ∫ ρ_k(t) Dg(x − t) dt and ‖Dψ_k(x)‖ ≤ ‖I‖ + ∫ ρ_k(t) ‖Dg(x − t)‖ dt ≤ 1 + A =: C (ρ_k ≥ 0, ∫ρ_k = 1).
7. Pointwise convergence. Fix x. Since rOut(β_k) = δ/(k+2) → 0 and g, Dg are continuous, (ρ_k ∗ g)(x) → g(x) and ∫ ρ_k(t) Dg(x − t) dt → Dg(x) (Mathlib ContDiffBump.convolution_tendsto_right_of_continuous; the derivative of step 6 is pointwise the same integral ∫ ρ_k(t) • Dg(x − t) dt as the scalar convolution ρ_k ⋆[lsmul ℝ ℝ, λ] Dg used by that lemma, by unfolding convolution_def; directly: |(ρ_k ∗ h)(x) − h(x)| ≤ sup_{|t| ≤ δ/(k+2)} |h(x − t) − h(x)| → 0 for h ∈ {g, Dg}). Hence ψ_k(x) = x + (ρ_k ∗ g)(x) → x + g(x) = φ(x) and Dψ_k(x) → I + Dg(x) = Dφ(x).
8. Conclusion: ψ_k, K' and C satisfy all requirements: K' compact ⊆ U (step 1), each ψ_k C^∞ (step 4), ψ_k = id off K' (step 5), ‖Dψ_k‖ ≤ C (step 6), and the two pointwise limits (step 7). (For P = 0 all statements are trivial: E is a point, g = 0 and ψ_k = id = φ. The Lean proof needs Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.BumpFunction.Normed and Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.BumpFunction.Convolution for ContDiffBump.normed and ContDiffBump.convolution_tendsto_right_of_continuous, which the submission may import although the frozen statement does not use them; the convolution derivative and smoothness lemmas are already in scope.)

d(ψ_k^#η) = ψ_k^#(dη), so 0 = ∂T(ψ_k^#η) = ∫_M θ ξ(dη(ψ_k x)∘Dψ_k(x)) dH^n.

subproblems.title: Simon 6.3.2(3): on open sets the mass of an integer multiplicity current equals its weight measure (reuse of the accepted declaration dtc_mass_eq_measure)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n) and R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity representation of T in U (IMRep U n with R.Represents T, i.e. T(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), where Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Then for every open W ⊆ U, M_W(T) = μ_R(W), where M_W(T) = T.massOn W is Simon's mass 6.2.5 with the Euclidean coefficient norm (the supremum of T(ω) over ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(y)| ≤ 1 for all y) and μ_R = θHⁿ⌞M = R.measure; both sides are taken in [0, ∞].
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U W : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → IsOpen W → W ⊆ U → R.Represents T → T.massOn W = R.measure W
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse: this is the comparator-accepted DAG declaration dtc_mass_eq_measure (node root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.mass_eq_measure-a1, accepted candidate commit bff81d3), whose frozen Lean type is reused verbatim; no new formal work is needed. It is the parent's resolved dependency mass_eq_measure; it is re-listed because the sibling carrier_facts uses it (parent step 1(b): μ_Y(ℝ^P ∖ K) = M_{ℝ^P∖K}(Y)). Its audited proof is reproduced below; in that text, "the parent proof" and "sibling" refer to the decomposition of root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1, in which it was proved, not to the present node.
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(3) (chapter-06.txt lines 763–766, stated there without proof) together with 2.4–2.8 (lines 222–283); this is the identity "M_W(S) = μ_S(W) for open W" quoted at the start of the parent proof. Notation: for α ∈ Λⁿ(ℝ^P) (Covector), |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_I α(e_{I(1)},…,e_{I(n)})²)^{1/2}, the sum over strictly increasing I : {1,…,n} → {1,…,P}; e^I ∈ Λⁿ is the covector e^I(v₁,…,vₙ) = det(⟨e_{I(a)}, v_b⟩)_{a,b}; μ := μ_R, so μ(B) = ∫_{M∩B} θ dHⁿ for Borel B. By definition M_W(T) = sup{ofReal T(ω) : ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω(y)| ≤ 1 ∀y} ("admissible" forms).
1. Algebraic lemma. Let τ₁,…,τₙ ∈ ℝ^P be orthonormal, σ ∈ {1, −1}, and let ζ ∈ Λₙ (MultiVector) satisfy ζ(α) = σ·α(τ₁,…,τₙ) for all α. For increasing I put d_I := det(⟨e_{I(a)}, τ_b⟩)_{a,b} = e^I(τ₁,…,τₙ). (a) Expanding each τ_b in the standard basis and using multilinearity and the alternating property (terms with a repeated basis vector vanish, the others are grouped by their increasing rearrangement with the sign of the sorting permutation) gives α(τ₁,…,τₙ) = Σ_I α(e_I)·d_I for every α. (b) By the Cauchy–Binet formula Σ_I d_I² = det(AᵀA), A the P×n matrix with columns τ_b; AᵀA = I_n by orthonormality, so Σ_I d_I² = 1. (c) Hence, by Cauchy–Schwarz, |ζ(α)| = |Σ_I α(e_I)d_I| ≤ |α| for every α. (d) Put α_ζ := Σ_I ζ(e^I)·e^I (a linear function of ζ). Since e^I(e_J) = δ_{IJ} for increasing I, J, α_ζ(e_J) = ζ(e^J) = σd_J, hence |α_ζ| = (Σ_J d_J²)^{1/2} = 1 and ζ(α_ζ) = Σ_I ζ(e^I)² = Σ_I d_I² = 1.
2. By the field `orients` of R there is an Hⁿ-null set Z ⊆ M such that for every x ∈ M ∖ Z, ξ(x) satisfies the hypothesis of step 1 (τ an orthonormal basis of the approximate tangent space T_xM). For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) the function x ↦ θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) is a.e. strongly measurable on M (ξ is, ω is continuous, evaluation is continuous bilinear) and bounded by θ(x)·sup|ω|·1_{tsupport ω}(x) off Z; since tsupport ω is a compact subset of U, ∫_{M∩tsupport ω} θ dHⁿ < ∞ (field `locallyIntegrable_mult`). So T(ω) is the integral of an integrable function.
3. Upper bound. Let ω be admissible. For x ∈ M ∖ Z, step 1(c) and tsupport ω ⊆ W give θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) ≤ θ(x)|ω(x)| ≤ θ(x)·1_W(x). Integrating, T(ω) ≤ ∫_{M∩W} θ dHⁿ = μ(W), so ofReal T(ω) ≤ μ(W). Taking the supremum, M_W(T) ≤ μ(W).
4. Lower bound on a compact set. Let K ⊆ W be compact and 0 < ε < 1. Fix s > 0 with K₁ := {y : dist(y, K) ≤ s} ⊆ W; K₁ is compact, K₁ ⊆ U, so μ(K₁) < ∞.
 (a) The open sets V_m := {dist(·, K) < 1/m} decrease to K and μ(K₁) < ∞, so for some m with 1/m < s the open set V := V_m satisfies K ⊆ V ⊆ K₁ and μ(V ∖ K) < ε.
 (b) Let α(y) := α_{ξ(y)} (step 1(d)); α is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, so there is a Borel map α̃ : ℝ^P → Λⁿ with α̃ = α μ-a.e. Since θ ≥ 1 on M, μ-null subsets of M are Hⁿ-null; let Z' be a Borel Hⁿ-null set containing Z ∪ ({α̃ ≠ α} ∩ M). For y ∈ M ∖ Z' we have |α̃(y)| = 1 and ξ(y)(α̃(y)) = 1. By Lusin's theorem for the finite Borel measure μ⌞K₁ on ℝ^P (Simon Ch. 1, 1.17; Λⁿ is identified with ℝ^{C(P,n)} through the coefficients α(e_I)) there is a compact F₀ ⊆ K with μ(K ∖ F₀) < ε/2 and α̃|_{F₀} continuous; by inner regularity there is a compact F ⊆ (F₀ ∩ M) ∖ Z' (a Borel set, M being Borel) with μ(((F₀ ∩ M) ∖ Z') ∖ F) < ε/2. As μ(ℝ^P ∖ M) = 0 and μ(Z') = 0, μ(K ∖ F) < ε; moreover F ⊆ M ∖ Z', α̃|_F is continuous, and |α̃| = 1, ξ(·)(α̃(·)) = 1 on F.
 (c) By the Tietze extension theorem (coefficientwise) α̃|_F extends to a continuous β₀ : ℝ^P → Λⁿ. Let r(v) := v / max(1, |v|), the continuous radial retraction of (Λⁿ, |·|) onto its closed unit ball, and β := r ∘ β₀. Then β is continuous, |β| ≤ 1, and β = α̃ on F (because |α̃| = 1 there).
 (d) Let φ_δ be a standard mollifier (smooth, ≥ 0, ∫φ_δ = 1, support in B_δ(0)) and β_δ := β * φ_δ (coefficientwise convolution). Then β_δ is smooth, |β_δ(y)| ≤ ∫|β(y − z)|φ_δ(z) dz ≤ 1 (convexity of the norm, Minkowski's integral inequality), and β_δ → β uniformly on compact sets as δ ↓ 0 (β is uniformly continuous on compact sets). Fix δ with |β_δ − β| ≤ ε on F.
 (e) Choose χ ∈ C_c^∞(V) with 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1 and χ = 1 on K (smooth Urysohn lemma), and set ω := χβ_δ. Then ω is smooth with compact tsupport ⊆ V ⊆ W ⊆ U, so ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), and |ω| ≤ 1: ω is admissible.
 (f) Since χ = 1 on F ⊆ K and ω = 0 off V, T(ω) = ∫_{F} θ ξ(β_δ) dHⁿ + ∫_{M∩(V∖F)} θ χ ξ(β_δ) dHⁿ. For y ∈ F (so y ∈ M ∖ Z'): ξ(y)(β_δ(y)) = ξ(y)(α̃(y)) + ξ(y)(β_δ(y) − β(y)) ≥ 1 − |β_δ(y) − β(y)| ≥ 1 − ε by step 1(c) and (b). For y ∈ (M ∩ (V ∖ F)) ∖ Z, |χ(y)ξ(y)(β_δ(y))| ≤ 1. Since μ(V ∖ F) ≤ μ(V ∖ K) + μ(K ∖ F) < 2ε, we get T(ω) ≥ (1 − ε)μ(F) − 2ε ≥ (1 − ε)(μ(K) − ε) − 2ε ≥ μ(K) − ε(μ(K) + 3).
 (g) Hence M_W(T) ≥ ofReal T(ω) ≥ μ(K) − ε(μ(K) + 3); letting ε ↓ 0 gives M_W(T) ≥ μ(K).
5. Exhaustion. W is open, so W = ⋃_m K_m with the increasing compact sets K_m := {y ∈ W : |y| ≤ m, dist(y, ℝ^P ∖ W) ≥ 1/m} (K_m := {|y| ≤ m} if W = ℝ^P). By continuity of μ from below and step 4, μ(W) = sup_m μ(K_m) ≤ M_W(T). Together with step 3, M_W(T) = μ(W) in [0, ∞].
proof_key_steps: A unit simple n-vector ζ satisfies |ζ(α)| ≤ |α|_Euclid (Cauchy–Binet) and has a dual covector α_ζ, linear in ζ, with |α_ζ| = 1 and ζ(α_ζ) = 1.
Upper bound: for every admissible ω, T(ω) ≤ ∫_{M∩W} θ dHⁿ = μ_R(W).
Lower bound on compact K ⊆ W: Lusin, Tietze, radial retraction, mollification and a cutoff give an admissible ω with T(ω) ≥ μ_R(K) − ε(μ_R(K) + 3).
Exhaust the open set W by compact sets to conclude M_W(T) = μ_R(W).

Source: Simon Ch. 6, 2.11 (definition of spt T, chapter-06.txt lines 297–301); the partition-of-unity argument below is the standard reason why the union in 2.11 is itself a set on which the current vanishes. Notation: "S vanishes on W" means S(η) = 0 for every η ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport η ⊆ W.
1. K := tsupport ω is compact and K ⊆ U, because ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) is a compactly supported smooth form with tsupport ω ⊆ U. If K = ∅ then ω = 0 and S(ω) = 0 by linearity; assume K ≠ ∅.
2. Since K ⊆ U and K ∩ spt S = ∅, we have K ⊆ U ∖ spt S ⊆ Z_S. By compactness there are finitely many open sets W₁,…,W_m from the family defining Z_S (each with S vanishing on W_i) such that K ⊆ W₁ ∪ … ∪ W_m.
3. Take a smooth partition of unity on ℝ^P subordinate to the open cover {W₁,…,W_m, ℝ^P ∖ K} (e.g. Mathlib's SmoothPartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate for the closed set K and the cover by W₁,…,W_m): smooth ψ₁,…,ψ_m : ℝ^P → [0,1] with tsupport ψ_i ⊆ W_i for each i and Σ_i ψ_i(y) = 1 for every y ∈ K.
4. For each i, ψ_iω (pointwise product of a smooth function and a smooth n-form) is smooth, and tsupport(ψ_iω) ⊆ tsupport ψ_i ∩ tsupport ω ⊆ W_i ∩ K; in particular it is compact and contained in U. Thus ψ_iω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport(ψ_iω) ⊆ W_i, and S(ψ_iω) = 0 since S vanishes on W_i.
5. ω = Σ_i ψ_iω pointwise: if ω(y) ≠ 0 then y ∈ K and Σ_iψ_i(y) = 1; if ω(y) = 0 both sides vanish. By linearity of S, S(ω) = Σ_i S(ψ_iω) = 0.
proof_key_steps: tsupport ω is a compact subset of the zero region of S, hence covered by finitely many open sets on which S vanishes.
A smooth partition of unity subordinate to this finite cover splits ω into test forms supported in those sets.
Each piece is annihilated by S; linearity gives S(ω) = 0.

subproblems.title: Carrier, mass and support facts for integer multiplicity currents in ℝ^P
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and write 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) for GeometricCurrentOn univ n. (1) Let Y ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) be represented by an integer multiplicity triple R = (M, θ, ξ) in ℝ^P (IMRep univ n, R.Represents Y), and let μ_R := θ·Hⁿ⌞M (R.measure, Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Then Hⁿ(M ∖ spt Y) = 0, the total mass satisfies M(Y) = μ_R(ℝ^P) (Y.mass = R.measure univ), and if spt Y is compact then μ_R(ℝ^P) < ∞. (2) For all Y₁, Y₂ ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P): spt Y₁ is closed, and spt(Y₁ − Y₂) ⊆ spt Y₁ ∪ spt Y₂, where Y₁ − Y₂ is the pointwise difference of currents.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ), (∀ (Y : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), R.Represents Y → μHE[n] (R.carrier \ Y.support) = 0 ∧ Y.mass = R.measure univ ∧ (IsCompact Y.support → R.measure univ ≠ ∞)) ∧ ∀ Y₁ Y₂ : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, IsClosed Y₁.support ∧ (Y₁ - Y₂).support ⊆ Y₁.support ∪ Y₂.support
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1(b)–(c) and 3(a) of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, 2.11 and Remark 3.2(3), chapter-06.txt lines 297–301 and 763–766). The frozen type is byte-identical to that of dimred_mbl_pf_imrep_carrier_mass_support in another branch.
Notation: Hⁿ := μHE[n]. For a representation R = (M, θ, ξ) (IMRep univ n), μ_R := R.measure = θ·Hⁿ⌞M, so μ_R(B) = ∫⁻_{M∩B} θ dHⁿ for Borel B. For a current Y ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P), spt Y = ℝ^P ∖ Z(Y), where the zero region Z(Y) is the union of all open W with closure(W) compact (and ⊆ ℝ^P) such that Y(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ W (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn.support and zeroRegion). M_W(Y) = Y.massOn W is the supremum of ofReal(Y(ω)) over the admissible ω (ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P), tsupport ω ⊆ W, covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(z)) ≤ 1 for all z), and M(Y) = Y.mass = Y.massOn ℝ^P.
1. Closedness. For every Y₁ ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P), Z(Y₁) is open, as a union of open sets (isOpen_zeroRegion); hence spt Y₁ = ℝ^P ∖ Z(Y₁) is closed. This is the first claim of part (2).
2. The mass vanishes off the support. Let Y be represented by R = (M, θ, ξ), K := spt Y and W := ℝ^P ∖ K, which is open by step 1. If ω is admissible for M_W(Y), then tsupport ω ⊆ W is disjoint from K = spt Y, so Y(ω) = 0 by the sibling vanish_off_support (U = ℝ^P, S = Y). Thus every element of the set whose supremum is M_W(Y) equals ofReal(0) = 0, and M_W(Y) = 0.
3. The carrier is null off the support. The sibling mass_eq_measure (U = ℝ^P open, W open, W ⊆ ℝ^P, R represents Y) gives μ_R(W) = M_W(Y) = 0, i.e. ∫⁻_{M∩W} θ dHⁿ = 0 (W is Borel). Since θ is ℕ-valued and θ(x) > 0 for x ∈ M (R.mult_pos), θ ≥ 1 on M, so Hⁿ(M ∩ W) = ∫⁻_{M∩W} 1 dHⁿ ≤ ∫⁻_{M∩W} θ dHⁿ = 0. As M ∖ spt Y = M ∩ W, Hⁿ(M ∖ spt Y) = 0.
4. Total mass. By definition M(Y) = M_{ℝ^P}(Y), and by mass_eq_measure with W = ℝ^P, M(Y) = μ_R(ℝ^P).
5. Finiteness for compact support. Suppose K = spt Y is compact. K is closed, hence Borel, so μ_R(ℝ^P) = μ_R(K) + μ_R(W) = μ_R(K) by step 3, and μ_R(K) = ∫⁻_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ by R.locallyIntegrable_mult applied to the compact set K ⊆ ℝ^P. Hence μ_R(ℝ^P) ≠ ∞. Steps 3–5 prove part (1).
6. Support of a difference. Let Y₁, Y₂ ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) and x ∈ ℝ^P with x ∉ spt Y₁ ∪ spt Y₂. Then x ∈ Z(Y₁) ∩ Z(Y₂): there are open sets W₁, W₂ containing x, with compact closures, such that Y_i(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ⊆ W_i (i = 1, 2). W := W₁ ∩ W₂ is open and contains x, and closure(W) ⊆ closure(W₁) is compact (a closed subset of a compact set) and contained in ℝ^P. If tsupport ω ⊆ W, then tsupport ω ⊆ W₁ and tsupport ω ⊆ W₂, so (Y₁ − Y₂)(ω) = Y₁(ω) − Y₂(ω) = 0 − 0 = 0 (the difference of currents in the contract's Sub instance is evaluated pointwise). Hence W is one of the sets forming Z(Y₁ − Y₂), x ∈ Z(Y₁ − Y₂) and x ∉ spt(Y₁ − Y₂). So spt(Y₁ − Y₂) ⊆ spt Y₁ ∪ spt Y₂, the second claim of part (2). ∎
proof_key_steps: Supports are complements of open zero regions, hence closed.
Y kills every admissible form supported in the open set ℝ^P ∖ spt Y (vanish_off_support), so M_{ℝ^P∖spt Y}(Y) = 0; by mass_eq_measure, ∫_{M∖spt Y} θ dHⁿ = 0 and, as θ ≥ 1 on M, Hⁿ(M ∖ spt Y) = 0.
mass_eq_measure with W = ℝ^P gives M(Y) = μ_R(ℝ^P); for compact spt Y, μ_R(ℝ^P) = μ_R(spt Y) = ∫_{M∩spt Y} θ dHⁿ < ∞.
A common relatively compact neighbourhood on which Y₁ and Y₂ vanish lies in the zero region of Y₁ − Y₂, so spt(Y₁ − Y₂) ⊆ spt Y₁ ∪ spt Y₂.

subproblems.title: Unit orientations under linear maps: |ξ(α∘L)| ≤ |α|_E·‖L‖ⁿ, and invariance when L fixes the oriented plane
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, Q ⊆ ℝ^P a linear subspace, ξ an n-vector (MultiVector P n, a continuous linear functional on n-covectors) that is a unit orientation of Q (IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q: there are an orthonormal family τ = (τ₁, …, τₙ) with span τ = Q and a sign s ∈ {1, −1} such that ξ(β) = s·β(τ₁, …, τₙ) for every n-covector β), and L : ℝ^P → ℝ^P a continuous linear map. For an n-covector α let α∘L be the n-covector (v₁, …, vₙ) ↦ α(Lv₁, …, Lvₙ) (α.compContinuousLinearMap L). Then (a) |ξ(α∘L)| ≤ |α|_E·‖L‖ⁿ for every n-covector α, where |·|_E is the Euclidean coefficient norm (covectorEuclideanNorm) and ‖L‖ the operator norm; and (b) if Lv = v for every v ∈ Q, then ξ(α∘L) = ξ(α) for every n-covector α.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (ξ : MultiVector P n) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (L : Euclid P →L[ℝ] Euclid P), IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q → (∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, |ξ (α.compContinuousLinearMap L)| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α * ‖L‖ ^ n) ∧ ((∀ v ∈ Q, L v = v) → ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, ξ (α.compContinuousLinearMap L) = ξ α)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1(a) of the parent proof (Cauchy–Binet, Cauchy–Schwarz and Hadamard; this is the pointwise estimate behind Simon Ch. 6, 2.27 and 2.29, chapter-06.txt lines 464–520, with Simon's Euclidean norm of 1.15). Part (b) is an elementary identity that this parent does not use; it is part of the frozen type so that the type is byte-identical to those of dimred_mbl_pf_unitOrientation_comp and dor_lmb_pc_unitOrientation_comp in other branches.
Notation: e₁, …, e_P the standard basis of ℝ^P. For an n-covector α and a strictly increasing I : {1, …, n} → {1, …, P}, α(e_I) := α(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(n)}); |α|_E := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_I α(e_I)²)^{1/2}. ‖L‖ is the operator norm. α∘L := α.compContinuousLinearMap L, so (α∘L)(v₁, …, vₙ) = α(Lv₁, …, Lvₙ). For v = (v₁, …, vₙ) in ℝ^P let V be the P×n matrix with entries V_{ij} = ⟨e_i, v_j⟩, V_I its n×n submatrix on the rows I(1), …, I(n), and Γ(v) := det(⟨v_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j} = det(VᵀV).
1. Expansion. Writing v_j = Σ_i V_{ij}e_i and expanding by multilinearity, α(v₁, …, vₙ) = Σ_{k : {1..n}→{1..P}} (Π_j V_{k(j)j})·α(e_{k(1)}, …, e_{k(n)}). Terms with k not injective vanish because α is alternating. Each injective k is uniquely I∘σ with I increasing and σ a permutation of {1, …, n}, and α(e_{I∘σ}) = sgn(σ)α(e_I). Grouping, α(v) = Σ_I α(e_I)·Σ_σ sgn(σ)Π_j V_{I(σ(j)),j} = Σ_I α(e_I)·det(V_I).
2. Cauchy–Schwarz. |α(v)| ≤ (Σ_I α(e_I)²)^{1/2}(Σ_I det(V_I)²)^{1/2} = |α|_E·(Σ_I det(V_I)²)^{1/2}.
3. Cauchy–Binet. Σ_I det(V_I)² = det(VᵀV) = Γ(v). Proof: det(VᵀV) is multilinear and alternating in the columns of the right factor V; expanding these columns in the standard basis exactly as in step 1 gives det(VᵀV) = Σ_I det((Vᵀ)^I)·det(V_I), where (Vᵀ)^I is the n×n submatrix of Vᵀ on the columns I, i.e. (V_I)ᵀ; so det(VᵀV) = Σ_I det(V_I)². Hence Γ(v) ≥ 0 and |α(v)| ≤ |α|_E·Γ(v)^{1/2}. (This is also the first part of the accepted declaration covectorEuclideanNorm_gram_bounds.)
4. Hadamard. Γ(v) ≤ Π_j |v_j|². If v₁, …, vₙ are linearly dependent, Vc = 0 for some c ≠ 0, so (VᵀV)c = 0 and Γ(v) = 0. Otherwise let σ₁, …, σₙ be the Gram–Schmidt orthonormalization of v₁, …, vₙ: v_j = Σ_{i≤j} T_{ij}σ_i with T upper triangular and T_{jj} = dist(v_j, span(v₁, …, v_{j−1})) ∈ (0, |v_j|]. Then ⟨v_i, v_j⟩ = (TᵀT)_{ij}, so Γ(v) = det(T)² = Π_j T_{jj}² ≤ Π_j |v_j|².
5. Set-up. By IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q there are an orthonormal family τ = (τ₁, …, τₙ) with span τ = Q and a sign s ∈ {1, −1} such that ξ(β) = s·β(τ₁, …, τₙ) for every n-covector β.
6. Part (a). Let α be an n-covector. Then ξ(α∘L) = s·(α∘L)(τ) = s·α(Lτ₁, …, Lτₙ). By steps 3 and 4 with v_j := Lτ_j, |ξ(α∘L)| = |α(Lτ₁, …, Lτₙ)| ≤ |α|_E·Γ(Lτ)^{1/2} ≤ |α|_E·Π_j|Lτ_j| ≤ |α|_E·Π_j ‖L‖·|τ_j| = |α|_E·‖L‖ⁿ, since |τ_j| = 1. (For n = 0 all products are empty, the empty I is the only increasing index, |α|_E = |α()| and ξ(α∘L) = s·(α∘L)() = s·α(): the inequality holds with equality.)
7. Part (b). Suppose Lv = v for every v ∈ Q. Each τ_j lies in span τ = Q, so Lτ_j = τ_j and (α∘L)(τ) = α(Lτ₁, …, Lτₙ) = α(τ₁, …, τₙ). Hence ξ(α∘L) = s·α(τ) = ξ(α) for every n-covector α. ∎
proof_key_steps: Expansion α(v) = Σ_I α(e_I)det(V_I) by multilinearity and the alternating property.
Cauchy–Schwarz and Cauchy–Binet: |α(v)| ≤ |α|_E·det(⟨v_i, v_j⟩)^{1/2}.
Hadamard (Gram–Schmidt): det(⟨v_i, v_j⟩) ≤ Π_j|v_j|²; with v_j = Lτ_j this gives |ξ(α∘L)| ≤ |α|_E‖L‖ⁿ.
If L fixes Q pointwise then L fixes each τ_j, so ξ(α∘L) = ±α(τ) = ξ(α).

subproblems.title: Representation-independent extension: the pulled-back integral is the limit of Y(ω_j) for a sequence of test forms chosen before Y and R
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, O ⊆ ℝ^P open, f : ℝ^P → ℝ^P of class C¹ on O (ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f O), K ⊆ O compact, and ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) (TestFormOn univ n). Then there is a sequence (ω_j)_{j∈ℕ} in 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) such that for every Y ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n) and every integer multiplicity triple R = (M, θ, ξ) in ℝ^P (IMRep univ n) representing Y with spt Y ⊆ K: Y(ω_j) → ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(f(x))∘Df(x)) dHⁿ(x) as j → ∞, where Hⁿ = μHE[n], Df(x) = fderiv ℝ f x and ω(f(x))∘Df(x) := (ω (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (O K : Set (Euclid P)) (f : Euclid P → Euclid P) (ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), IsOpen O → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f O → IsCompact K → K ⊆ O → ∃ ωs : ℕ → TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, ∀ (Y : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), R.Represents Y → Y.support ⊆ K → Tendsto (fun j => Y (ωs j)) atTop (𝓝 (∫ x in R.carrier, (R.mult x : ℝ) * R.orient x (((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x)) ∂μHE[n]))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2(c) and 3(b) of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, 2.23–2.24(2), chapter-06.txt lines 404–425: f_#T(ω) = T(ζ·f^#ω) with ζ = 1 near spt T, and its integral form for currents of locally finite mass). The parent approximates the continuous, compactly supported form β = χ·(ω(f(·))∘ΛⁿDf(·)) uniformly by mollified smooth forms β_k with supports in a fixed compact set, and identifies ∫_M θ⟨β, ξ⟩ dHⁿ with lim_k Y(β_k). Here the sequence is fixed before Y and R are chosen; this yields both the independence of the representation (2(c)) and the additivity (3(b)) in the parent. The frozen type is byte-identical to that of dimred_mbl_pf_pullback_integral_extension in another branch.
Notation: Hⁿ := μHE[n]; ‖·‖ is the operator norm on n-covectors (a finite-dimensional normed space); for x ∈ ℝ^P, γ(x) := ω(f(x))∘Df(x) = (ω (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x).
1. γ is continuous on O. f is C¹ on the open set O, so f and Df are continuous on O (ContDiffOn.continuousOn and ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen with 1 ≤ 1). ω is continuous (it is smooth). The map (β, A) ↦ β∘A from n-covectors × linear maps to n-covectors is continuous: it is β ↦ ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMapCLM A β, which is jointly continuous in (β, A) (equivalently, in coordinates it is a polynomial in the entries of β and A). Hence γ is continuous on O.
2. Cut-off. K is compact, O open and K ⊆ O, so there is δ > 0 with cthickening(2δ, K) ⊆ O (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). By the smooth Urysohn lemma (exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff with the open set thickening(2δ, K) and the closed set cthickening(δ, K) contained in it) there is χ : ℝ^P → [0, 1] of class C^∞ with χ = 1 on cthickening(δ, K) ⊇ W₀ := thickening(δ, K) ⊇ K and tsupport χ ⊆ cthickening(2δ, K), a compact subset of O. (This is the cut-off of the parent's step 2(c); the same construction appears in the sibling c1_perturbation, which is not needed here.) Define h(x) := χ(x)·γ(x) for x ∈ ℝ^P. Then:
 (a) h is continuous on ℝ^P: on the open set O it is the product of the continuous functions χ and γ (step 1); on the open set ℝ^P ∖ tsupport χ it vanishes identically; and these two open sets cover ℝ^P because tsupport χ ⊆ O.
 (b) h(x) = 0 for x ∉ tsupport χ, so h has compact support; put B := sup_x ‖h(x)‖ < ∞.
 (c) h = γ on W₀, in particular on K.
3. The test forms. For j ∈ ℕ let ρ_j : ℝ^P → ℝ be C^∞ with ρ_j ≥ 0, ∫ρ_j = 1 and support in the open ball of radius r_j := 1/(j + 1) about 0 (the normalized ContDiffBump with outer radius r_j), and let ω_j := ρ_j ∗ h, i.e. ω_j(x) = ∫ ρ_j(t)·h(x − t) dt (convolution of a scalar kernel with a covector-valued function; ℝ^P carries Lebesgue measure).
 (a) ω_j is C^∞ (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left: ρ_j is C^∞ with compact support and h is continuous, hence locally integrable) and has compact support (contained in tsupport h + closedBall(0, 1)); so ω_j ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) (IsTestForm, and tsupport ω_j ⊆ ℝ^P trivially).
 (b) Since ρ_j ≥ 0 and ∫ρ_j = 1, ‖ω_j(x)‖ ≤ B and ‖ω_j(x) − h(x)‖ ≤ sup_{|t| < r_j} ‖h(x − t) − h(x)‖ for every x (ContDiffBump.dist_normed_convolution_le). h is uniformly continuous (continuous with compact support), so δ_j := sup_x ‖ω_j(x) − h(x)‖ → 0 as j → ∞.
 (c) The sequence (ω_j) depends only on f, ω, O and K (through δ and χ), not on any current or representation.
4. Let Y ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) and R = (M, θ, ξ) (IMRep univ n) with R.Represents Y and spt Y ⊆ K.
 (a) By the sibling carrier_facts (part (1)), Hⁿ(M ∖ spt Y) = 0; as M ∖ K ⊆ M ∖ spt Y, Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0.
 (b) By R.locallyIntegrable_mult for the compact set K, c := ∫⁻_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞.
 (c) By R.orients, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M there are an orthonormal family τ and s ∈ {1, −1} with ξ(x)(β) = s·β(τ) for every n-covector β; at such x, |ξ(x)(β)| = |β(τ)| ≤ ‖β‖·Π_i|τ_i| = ‖β‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm).
5. Rewriting both sides. Since R represents Y and ω_j ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P), Y(ω_j) = R.action ω_j = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω_j(x)) dHⁿ(x). Since h = γ on K and Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0, the functions x ↦ θ(x)ξ(x)(γ(x)) and x ↦ θ(x)ξ(x)(h(x)) agree Hⁿ⌞M-a.e., so their integrals over M coincide (integral_congr_ae; this needs no integrability). The functions θ·ξ(ω_j) and θ·ξ(h) are a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M (θ is measurable, ξ is a.e. strongly measurable, ω_j and h are continuous, and evaluation (ζ, β) ↦ ζ(β) is continuous bilinear), and by step 4 they are bounded Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. by B·θ·1_K, whose integral is B·c < ∞; so they are integrable.
6. Convergence. By linearity of ξ(x) and of the integral, |Y(ω_j) − ∫_M θ(x)ξ(x)(γ(x)) dHⁿ(x)| = |∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω_j(x) − h(x)) dHⁿ(x)| ≤ ∫_M θ(x)·‖ω_j(x) − h(x)‖·1_K(x) dHⁿ(x) ≤ δ_j·c → 0, using step 4(c) and Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0. Hence Y(ω_j) → ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(f(x))∘Df(x)) dHⁿ(x) as j → ∞, for every such Y and R and with the same sequence (ω_j). ∎
proof_key_steps: γ = ω(f(·))∘Df(·) is continuous on O; a smooth cut-off χ (χ = 1 near K, compact tsupport χ ⊆ O) makes h = χγ a continuous compactly supported form equal to γ on K.
Mollifications ω_j = ρ_j ∗ h are test forms converging uniformly to h; they depend only on f, ω, O, K.
For every R representing Y with spt Y ⊆ K: Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0 (carrier_facts), ∫_{M∩K} θ < ∞, and |ξ(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖ a.e.
Y(ω_j) = ∫_M θξ(ω_j), ∫_M θξ(γ) = ∫_M θξ(h), and the difference is at most ∫_{M∩K}θ·sup‖ω_j − h‖ → 0.

subproblems.title: Mass bound M(Z) ≤ Lⁿ·M(Y) for a current Z given by the push-forward formula
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, O ⊆ ℝ^P, f : ℝ^P → ℝ^P and L ∈ ℝ with ‖Df(y)‖ ≤ L for every y ∈ O (Df(y) = fderiv ℝ f y, operator norm). Let Y, Z ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n) and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity triple in ℝ^P (IMRep univ n) representing Y, with spt Y compact and spt Y ⊆ O. Suppose Z(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(f(x))∘Df(x)) dHⁿ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) (Hⁿ = μHE[n], ω(f(x))∘Df(x) := (ω (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x)). Then M(Z) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(Lⁿ)·M(Y) for the total masses (Z.mass ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (L ^ n) * Y.mass).

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, 2.27 and 2.29: M_W(f_#T) ≤ (ess sup |Df|)ⁿ·M_{f⁻¹(W)}(T), chapter-06.txt lines 464–520), applied to any current Z given by the push-forward formula, together with the parent's remark that L ≥ 0 when O ≠ ∅ while O = ∅ forces spt Y = ∅. Notation: Hⁿ := μHE[n]; |·|_E := covectorEuclideanNorm; R = (M, θ, ξ); μ_R := R.measure = θ·Hⁿ⌞M; K := spt Y; M(·) is the mass, the local mass on the whole domain ℝ^P (massOn univ), i.e. the supremum of ofReal(T(ω)) over ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) with |ω(z)|_E ≤ 1 for all z.

2. Case L < 0. If y ∈ O, then 0 ≤ ‖Df(y)‖ ≤ L < 0, which is impossible; so O = ∅, hence K = ∅ (K ⊆ O) and Hⁿ(M) = Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0. Then Hⁿ⌞M is the zero measure, every integral over M vanishes, Z(ω) = 0 for every ω, and M(Z) = sup ofReal(0) = 0 ≤ ofReal(Lⁿ)·M(Y). From now on L ≥ 0.

Notation. Hⁿ := μHE[n]; on ℝⁿ = Euclid n it is Lebesgue measure Lⁿ (du). M = R.carrier, θ = R.mult, ξ = R.orient. e₁, …, eₙ is the standard basis of ℝⁿ. For an n-covector β, |β|_E := covectorEuclideanNorm β, ‖β‖ is its operator norm, and ⟨β, ζ⟩ := ζ(β) for an n-vector ζ. For a linear A : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P, A_#e is the n-vector β ↦ β(Ae₁, …, Aeₙ) and J_A := det(⟨Ae_i, Ae_j⟩)_{i,j}^{1/2} ≥ 0 (the area Jacobian, equal to LinearMap.normDet of A and to SimonGMT areaJacobianAt at differentiability points). For G : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P differentiable at u, J_G(u) := J_{DG(u)}. For orthonormal σ = (σ₁, …, σₙ), σ_# is the n-vector β ↦ β(σ₁, …, σₙ), a unit orientation of span σ. n ≥ 1 by hypothesis.

Algebra.
(A0) For an n-covector β and v₁, …, vₙ ∈ ℝ^P: |β(v)| ≤ |β|_E·det(⟨v_i, v_j⟩)^{1/2} ≤ |β|_E·Π_j|v_j|; for orthonormal σ also |β(σ)| ≤ |β|_E and |β(σ)| ≤ ‖β‖. Proof: expanding v_j in the standard basis of ℝ^P, multilinearity and the alternating property give β(v) = Σ_I β(e_I)·det(V_I) (I increasing, V_I the n×n minor of the matrix of v on the rows I); Cauchy–Schwarz and the Cauchy–Binet formula Σ_I det(V_I)² = det(VᵀV) = det(⟨v_i, v_j⟩) give the first inequality; Hadamard's inequality det(⟨v_i, v_j⟩) ≤ Π_j|v_j|² (zero for dependent v; for independent v, Gram–Schmidt writes VᵀV = TᵀT with T upper triangular and T_jj ≤ |v_j|) gives the second; for orthonormal σ the Gram determinant is 1, and |β(σ)| ≤ ‖β‖·Π_j|σ_j| = ‖β‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm).
(A1) Two unit orientations of the same n-dimensional subspace differ by a sign, and −ζ is a unit orientation of Q whenever ζ is. Proof: if τ, τ' are orthonormal bases of Q, then τ'_i = Σ_j O_ij τ_j with O orthogonal, and multilinear alternating expansion gives β(τ') = det(O)·β(τ) with det O = ±1; the definition of IsUnitOrientationOf allows either sign.
(A2) Let A : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P be linear. If A is injective, let σ be the Gram–Schmidt orthonormalization of Ae₁, …, Aeₙ: Ae_j = Σ_{i≤j} T_ij σ_i with T upper triangular and T_jj > 0. Then (⟨Ae_i, Ae_j⟩) = TᵀT, so J_A = det T > 0, and multilinear alternating expansion gives β(Ae₁, …, Aeₙ) = det(T)·β(σ) for every β, i.e. A_#e = J_A·σ_#, where σ_# is a unit orientation of span σ = A(ℝⁿ), an n-dimensional subspace. If A is not injective, Ae₁, …, Aeₙ are linearly dependent, so A_#e = 0 (β alternating) and J_A = 0 (singular Gram matrix). In both cases |⟨β, A_#e⟩| ≤ J_A·|β|_E (A0), and J_A ≤ Π_j|Ae_j| ≤ ‖A‖ⁿ.
(A3) For linear A : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P and L : ℝ^P → ℝ^P: (LA)_#e is the n-vector β ↦ (β∘L)(Ae₁, …, Aeₙ), and J_{LA} ≤ ‖L‖ⁿ·J_A. Proof of the inequality: if A is not injective, neither is LA, and both sides vanish. Otherwise, with σ and T from (A2) and the isometry V : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P, Ve_i := σ_i, we have A = V∘T, so (⟨LAe_i, LAe_j⟩) = Tᵀ·(⟨Lσ_i, Lσ_j⟩)·T, J_{LA} = det(T)·J_{LV} = J_A·J_{LV}, and J_{LV} ≤ Π_i|Lσ_i| ≤ ‖L‖ⁿ by (A2).

1. Reductions.
(a) M₁ := M ∩ K is Borel, Hⁿ(M ∖ M₁) = 0 by hypothesis, and Hⁿ(M₁) ≤ ∫⁻_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ (θ ≥ 1 on M; R.locallyIntegrable_mult for the compact set K ⊆ U).
(b) Cut-off of f. Choose δ > 0 with cthickening(2δ, K) ⊆ O (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open) and a C^∞ function χ : ℝ^P → [0, 1] with χ = 1 on W₀ := thickening(δ, K) ⊇ K and tsupport χ ⊆ cthickening(2δ, K), a compact subset of O (smooth Urysohn lemma, exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff). Put f̂(x) := x + χ(x)·(f(x) − x). Then f̂ is C¹ on ℝ^P (at points of O because f is C¹ on the open set O; near points outside tsupport χ because f̂ = id there; these two open sets cover ℝ^P), f̂ = id off the compact set tsupport χ, and f̂ = f on the open set W₀, so f̂(x) = f(x) and Df̂(x) = Df(x) for x ∈ K (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq). Df̂ is continuous and equals the identity off a compact set, so Λ := max(1, sup_x ‖Df̂(x)‖) < ∞, and f̂ is Λ-Lipschitz on ℝ^P (mean value inequality on the convex set ℝ^P). Since Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0, for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U): Q(ω) = ∫_{M₁} F_ω dHⁿ, where F_ω(x) := θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(f̂(x))∘Df̂(x)) (the integrands agree Hⁿ⌞M-a.e.). Also f̂(M₁) ⊆ f̂(K) = f(K) ⊆ U.
(c) Integrability. By R.orients and (A0), |ξ(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖ for every β, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M; with ‖β∘A‖ ≤ ‖β‖·‖A‖ⁿ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.norm_compContinuousLinearMap_le), |F_ω| ≤ ‖ω‖_∞Λⁿθ Hⁿ-a.e. on M₁, where ‖ω‖_∞ := sup_z ‖ω(z)‖ < ∞. F_ω is a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M (θ measurable, ξ a.e. strongly measurable, x ↦ ω(f̂(x))∘Df̂(x) continuous), hence Hⁿ⌞M₁-integrable. Fix a Borel map ξ̃ with ξ̃ = ξ Hⁿ-a.e. on M (a.e. strong measurability).
(d) Good points. By (TL) with (U, A, B) := (U, M₁, M) (Borel sets, M₁ ⊆ M ⊆ U, Hⁿ(M ∩ C) ≤ ∫⁻_{M∩C} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for compact C ⊆ U), for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M₁ the sets M and M₁ have the same approximate tangent spaces at x. With R.orients: for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M₁ there is a subspace T_x with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M₁ x T_x and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(x)) T_x, and ξ̃(x) = ξ(x). Such x are called good. Approximate tangent spaces are unique when they exist (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique).

2. Parametrization of M₁ (parent 6(a)–(b); the comparator-accepted DAG declaration dpf_rectifiable_bilipschitz_pieces states exactly this conclusion for Borel countably n-rectifiable sets, and a decomposition of this node may reuse it). There are Lipschitz maps G_i : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P, Borel sets A_i ⊆ ℝⁿ and constants κ_i > 0 (i ∈ ℕ) such that κ_i|u − v| ≤ |G_i(u) − G_i(v)| for u, v ∈ A_i, G_i is differentiable at every u ∈ A_i with DG_i(u) injective, the sets G_i(A_i) are Borel, contained in M₁ and pairwise disjoint, and Hⁿ(M₁ ∖ ⋃_i G_i(A_i)) = 0. Proof.
 (i) M₁ ⊆ M is countably n-rectifiable (R.rectifiable, CountablyRectifiable.mono): M₁ ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝⁿ) with Hⁿ(M₀) = 0 and F_j : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P Lipschitz.
 (ii) By Rademacher's theorem (LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt), the set D_j of differentiability points of F_j is Borel with Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ D_j) = 0, so Hⁿ(F_j(ℝⁿ ∖ D_j)) = 0 (Lipschitz images of null sets are null, LipschitzWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le, with μHE[n] = Lⁿ on ℝⁿ).
 (iii) Z_j := {u ∈ D_j : DF_j(u) not injective} satisfies Hⁿ(F_j(Z_j)) = 0 (the area formula with vanishing Jacobian; SimonGMT area_image_criticalSet_eq_zero).
 (iv) E_j := (D_j ∖ Z_j) ∩ F_j⁻¹(M₁) is Borel (u ↦ DF_j(u) is Borel on D_j, measurable_fderiv; injectivity of DF_j(u) means det(⟨DF_j(u)e_p, DF_j(u)e_q⟩) ≠ 0). For an injective linear A : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P choose c_A > 0 with |Aw| ≥ c_A|w| for all w, and put r(A) := c_A/2; put r(A) := 1 for non-injective A. The partition lemma exists_partition_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt (applied to F_j on E_j with derivative DF_j and the positive function r) gives pairwise disjoint Borel sets t_l covering E_j and linear maps A_l, each equal to DF_j(y_l) for some y_l ∈ E_j (hence injective), such that |F_j(u) − F_j(v) − A_l(u − v)| ≤ r(A_l)|u − v| for u, v ∈ E_j ∩ t_l; therefore |F_j(u) − F_j(v)| ≥ (c_{A_l}/2)|u − v| there.
 (v) Enumerate the pieces E_j ∩ t_l (over all j, l) as E'_i, with G_i := F_j and κ_i := c_{A_l}/2. G_i is continuous and injective on the Borel set E'_i, so every G_i(S) with S ⊆ E'_i Borel is Borel (Lusin–Souslin, MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn). Disjointify: A_i := E'_i ∖ G_i⁻¹(⋃_{i'<i} G_{i'}(A_{i'})), recursively; the A_i are Borel, the G_i(A_i) ⊆ M₁ are pairwise disjoint Borel sets, and ⋃_i G_i(A_i) = ⋃_i G_i(E'_i).
 (vi) M₁ ∖ ⋃_i G_i(A_i) ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝⁿ ∖ D_j) ∪ ⋃_j F_j(Z_j), which is Hⁿ-null. ∎
 Null-set transfer: (G_i|A_i)⁻¹ : G_i(A_i) → A_i is κ_i⁻¹-Lipschitz, so Lⁿ(A_i ∩ G_i⁻¹(Z)) ≤ κ_i^{−n}·Hⁿ(Z) for Z ⊆ G_i(A_i) (LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le), and Hⁿ(G_i(N)) ≤ Lip(G_i)ⁿ·Lⁿ(N) for N ⊆ ℝⁿ. Hence a property holds at Hⁿ-a.e. point of G_i(A_i) iff it holds at G_i(u) for Lⁿ-a.e. u ∈ A_i. The same transfer applies to every bi-Lipschitz piece below.

3. Lemma T (approximate tangent planes of bi-Lipschitz images). Let A ⊆ ℝⁿ be Borel, G : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P Lipschitz and differentiable at every u ∈ A, and κ > 0 with κ|u − v| ≤ |G(u) − G(v)| for u, v ∈ A. Then for Lⁿ-a.e. u ∈ A, DG(u) is injective and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (G(A)) (G(u)) (DG(u)(ℝⁿ)). Proof.
 (i) The set of differentiability points of G is Borel and u ↦ DG(u) is Borel on it (measurableSet_of_differentiableAt, measurable_fderiv), with ‖DG(u)‖ ≤ Lip(G); so F := 1_A·J_G is Borel and bounded by Lip(G)ⁿ (A2), hence locally integrable. By the Lebesgue density theorem (Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div) and the Lebesgue differentiation theorem (ae_tendsto_average_norm_sub), Lⁿ-a.e. u ∈ A is a density point of A and satisfies ⨍_{B_s(u)} |F(v) − F(u)| dv → 0 as s ↓ 0. Fix such u ∈ A; then F(u) = J_G(u).
 (ii) |DG(u)w| ≥ κ|w| for every w; in particular DG(u) is injective. Let w ≠ 0 and 0 < ε < 1. For all small r > 0 the ball B(u + rw, εr|w|) meets A: otherwise B(u, (1 + ε)r|w|) ∖ A would contain it, a fixed fraction (ε/(1 + ε))ⁿ > 0 of the volume of B(u, (1 + ε)r|w|), contradicting density 1 at u. Pick v_r ∈ A in that ball, so |v_r − u − rw| < εr|w| and |v_r − u| ≥ (1 − ε)r|w|. Differentiability at u gives |G(v_r) − G(u) − DG(u)(v_r − u)| = o(r), hence r|DG(u)w| ≥ |DG(u)(v_r − u)| − ‖DG(u)‖εr|w| ≥ |G(v_r) − G(u)| − o(r) − ‖DG(u)‖εr|w| ≥ κ(1 − ε)r|w| − ‖DG(u)‖εr|w| − o(r). Dividing by r and letting r ↓ 0 and then ε ↓ 0 gives |DG(u)w| ≥ κ|w|. So V_u := DG(u)(ℝⁿ) is n-dimensional and J_G(u) > 0.
 (iii) Blow-ups. Put x := G(u), η_r(y) := r⁻¹(y − x) (SimonGMT blowUpMap x r), and let h ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) vanish outside B_ρ(0). G(A) is Borel (Lusin–Souslin). Scaling: η_r is a translation (an isometry) followed by the homothety of ratio r⁻¹, so Hⁿ(η_r(S)) = r^{−n}·Hⁿ(S) for every S ⊆ ℝ^P (Mathlib Isometry.hausdorffMeasure_image and MeasureTheory.Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀; μHE[n] is a fixed multiple of μH[n]). Hence the image of Hⁿ⌞S under η_r is rⁿ·Hⁿ⌞η_r(S) (for Borel B, Hⁿ(S ∩ η_r⁻¹(B)) = Hⁿ(η_r⁻¹(η_r(S) ∩ B)) = rⁿ·Hⁿ(η_r(S) ∩ B)), i.e. ∫_{η_r(S)} h dHⁿ = r^{−n}·∫_S h∘η_r dHⁿ for Borel S. By the scaling of Hⁿ under the similarity η_r and the injective area formula for the Lipschitz map G on the Borel set A (SimonGMT weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_injOn applied to the positive and negative parts of h∘η_r; its Jacobian areaJacobianAt G v equals J_G(v) for v ∈ A), followed by the substitution v = u + rw (dv = rⁿdw):
 I(r) := ∫_{η_r(G(A))} h dHⁿ = r^{−n}∫_A h((G(v) − x)/r)·J_G(v) dv = ∫_{ℝⁿ} F(u + rw)·h(D_r(w)) dw, where D_r(w) := (G(u + rw) − G(u))/r.
 If u + rw ∈ A then |D_r(w)| ≥ κ|w|, so the last integrand vanishes unless |w| < ρ' := ρ/κ; likewise h(DG(u)w) = 0 for |w| ≥ ρ' by (ii). Hence, with B' := B_{ρ'}(0) ⊆ ℝⁿ,
 |I(r) − J_G(u)·∫_{ℝⁿ} h(DG(u)w) dw| ≤ sup|h|·∫_{B'} |F(u + rw) − F(u)| dw + J_G(u)·Lⁿ(B')·sup_{w∈B'} |h(D_r(w)) − h(DG(u)w)|.
 The first term equals sup|h|·Lⁿ(B')·⨍_{B_{rρ'}(u)} |F − F(u)| → 0 by (i); the second tends to 0 because D_r → DG(u) uniformly on B' (differentiability at u) and h is uniformly continuous. Finally J_G(u)·∫_{ℝⁿ} h(DG(u)w) dw = ∫_{V_u} h dHⁿ: by the linear area formula (SimonGMT linear_area_formula, i.e. Mathlib LinearMap.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image) Hⁿ(DG(u)(S)) = J_G(u)·Lⁿ(S) for every S ⊆ ℝⁿ, so Hⁿ⌞V_u is the image of J_G(u)·Lⁿ under the injective linear map DG(u) onto V_u, and integrating h gives the identity. Since finrank V_u = n and h is arbitrary, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (G(A)) x V_u. ∎
 Remark (reuse; not a proof step). In both applications below (G_i on A_i in step 4 and H_i on A_il in step 9) the derivative is injective at every point of the piece by construction, so the instance of Lemma T that is used is exactly the statement of the DAG node ptd_piece_image_approxTangent_ae (not yet accepted), which a decomposition of this node may reuse once it is accepted.

4. Tangent planes and orientation along the pieces (parent 6(b); Simon 3.4–3.5). Fix i. By (TL) with (U, A, B) := (U, G_i(A_i), M₁) (Borel, G_i(A_i) ⊆ M₁ ⊆ U, Hⁿ(M₁) < ∞), for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ G_i(A_i) the sets G_i(A_i) and M₁ have the same approximate tangent spaces at x. Combining this with step 1(d), Lemma T for (A_i, G_i, κ_i), uniqueness of approximate tangent spaces and the null-set transfer of step 2: for Lⁿ-a.e. u ∈ A_i, the point x := G_i(u) is good, T_x = DG_i(u)(ℝⁿ), and ξ(x) = ξ̃(x) is a unit orientation of it. By (A2), DG_i(u)_#e/J_{G_i}(u) is also a unit orientation of DG_i(u)(ℝⁿ), so by (A1)
 (★) ξ(G_i(u)) = s_i(u)·DG_i(u)_#e/J_{G_i}(u), s_i(u) ∈ {1, −1},
 for Lⁿ-a.e. u ∈ A_i, where s_i(u) := 1 if ξ̃(G_i(u)) = DG_i(u)_#e/J_{G_i}(u) and s_i(u) := −1 otherwise (a Borel function on A_i). Put θ_i := θ∘G_i on A_i; θ_i ≥ 1 there, since G_i(A_i) ⊆ M.

5. The maps H_i := f̂∘G_i (parent 6(b): d^M f_{x#}ξ(x) = Df(x)_#ξ(x)). H_i : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P is Lipschitz and differentiable at every u ∈ A_i with DH_i(u) = Df̂(G_i(u))∘DG_i(u) (chain rule). By (★), for Lⁿ-a.e. u ∈ A_i and every n-covector β: ξ(G_i(u))(β∘Df̂(G_i(u))) = s_i(u)·β(Df̂(G_i(u))DG_i(u)e₁, …, Df̂(G_i(u))DG_i(u)eₙ)/J_{G_i}(u) = s_i(u)·⟨β, DH_i(u)_#e⟩/J_{G_i}(u); and by (A3), J_{H_i}(u) ≤ ‖Df̂(G_i(u))‖ⁿ·J_{G_i}(u) ≤ Λⁿ·J_{G_i}(u).

6. Pulling Q back (parent 6(c); Simon 3.3 and 3.6). Fix ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). By step 1(b)–(c) and step 2 (disjoint Borel pieces covering M₁ up to a null set, F_ω integrable), Q(ω) = Σ_i ∫_{G_i(A_i)} F_ω dHⁿ, absolutely convergent. The injective area formula for G_i on A_i (weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_injOn applied to the positive and negative parts of a Borel version of F_ω, which are integrable; by the null-set transfer of step 2 the choice of version does not matter. The same passage from the nonnegative area formula to integrable signed integrands is the content of the accepted DAG declaration dpfir_integral_eq_of_area_lintegral, which a decomposition of this node may reuse) and step 5 give
 ∫_{G_i(A_i)} F_ω dHⁿ = ∫_{A_i} F_ω(G_i(u))·J_{G_i}(u) du = ∫_{A_i} θ_i(u)·s_i(u)·⟨ω(H_i(u)), DH_i(u)_#e⟩ du,
 since F_ω(G_i(u)) = θ_i(u)·ξ(G_i(u))(ω(H_i(u))∘Df̂(G_i(u))). By (A2), |⟨ω(H_i(u)), DH_i(u)_#e⟩| ≤ |ω|_{E,∞}·J_{H_i}(u) with |ω|_{E,∞} := sup_z |ω(z)|_E, and by step 5 and the area formula, Σ_i ∫_{A_i} θ_i J_{H_i} du ≤ Λⁿ·Σ_i ∫_{A_i} θ_i J_{G_i} du = Λⁿ·∫_{M₁} θ dHⁿ < ∞.

7. Removing the critical part; bi-Lipschitz pieces of H_i (parent 6(c); Simon 3.4). A_i⁺ := {u ∈ A_i : DH_i(u) injective} is Borel. For u ∈ A_i ∖ A_i⁺, DH_i(u)_#e = 0 by (A2), so the integrand of step 6 vanishes there (these are the points with J^M f = 0). Exactly as in step 2(iv) (partition lemma with r(A) = c_A/2, applied to H_i on A_i⁺ with the derivative DH_i, which is injective there), A_i⁺ is the disjoint union of countably many Borel sets A_il with κ_il|u − v| ≤ |H_i(u) − H_i(v)| for u, v ∈ A_il, κ_il > 0. Hence ∫_{A_i} θ_i s_i ⟨ω∘H_i, DH_i_#e⟩ du = Σ_l ∫_{A_il} θ_i s_i ⟨ω∘H_i, DH_i_#e⟩ du.

8. Image pieces (Simon 3.6). N_il := H_i(A_il) is Borel (Lusin–Souslin), H_i|A_il is injective with κ_il⁻¹-Lipschitz inverse, and N_il ⊆ f̂(M₁) ⊆ f(K) ⊆ U. On N_il define g_il := (θ_i·s_i)∘(H_i|A_il)⁻¹, an integer-valued Borel function with |g_il| ≥ 1, and η_il := (DH_i(·)_#e/J_{H_i}(·))∘(H_i|A_il)⁻¹, Borel; for u ∈ A_il, DH_i(u)_#e/J_{H_i}(u) is a unit orientation of DH_i(u)(ℝⁿ) by (A2). Since ⟨ω(H_i(u)), DH_i(u)_#e⟩ = J_{H_i}(u)·⟨ω(H_i(u)), η_il(H_i(u))⟩, the injective area formula for H_i on A_il gives
 ∫_{A_il} θ_i s_i ⟨ω∘H_i, DH_i_#e⟩ du = ∫_{N_il} g_il(y)·⟨ω(y), η_il(y)⟩ dHⁿ(y),
 and Σ_{i,l} ∫_{N_il} |g_il| dHⁿ = Σ_{i,l} ∫_{A_il} θ_i J_{H_i} du ≤ Λⁿ·∫_{M₁} θ dHⁿ < ∞ (step 6). With steps 6–7, Q(ω) = Σ_{i,l} ∫_{N_il} g_il⟨ω, η_il⟩ dHⁿ, absolutely convergent (|⟨ω, η_il⟩| ≤ |ω|_{E,∞} by (A0)). Put N := ⋃_{i,l} N_il: N is Borel, N ⊆ U, and Hⁿ(N) ≤ Σ_{i,l} Hⁿ(N_il) ≤ Σ_{i,l} ∫_{N_il} |g_il| dHⁿ < ∞.

9. Common tangent planes (parent 6(d); Simon 3.7). Fix (i, l). Lemma T for (A_il, H_i, κ_il) and the null-set transfer give: for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ N_il, with u := (H_i|A_il)⁻¹(y), N_il has the approximate tangent space DH_i(u)(ℝⁿ) at y. (TL) with (U, A, B) := (ℝ^P, N_il, N) (Borel, N_il ⊆ N, Hⁿ(N) < ∞) shows that for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ N_il the sets N_il and N have the same approximate tangent spaces at y. Discarding countably many null sets: for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ N and every (i, l) with y ∈ N_il, N has the approximate tangent space T_yN = DH_i((H_i|A_il)⁻¹(y))(ℝⁿ) at y (unique), and η_il(y) is a unit orientation of T_yN. Fix an enumeration of ℕ × ℕ and let η(y) := η_{i₀l₀}(y) for the first (i₀, l₀) with y ∈ N_{i₀l₀}; η is Borel on N. By (A1), η_il(y) = ε_il(y)·η(y) with ε_il(y) ∈ {1, −1}, where ε_il(y) := 1 if η_il(y) = η(y) and −1 otherwise (Borel).

10. Integer multiplicity (parent 6(e); Simon 3.8). The function Σ_{i,l} |g_il|·1_{N_il} is integrable (step 8), hence finite Hⁿ-a.e.; since |g_il| ≥ 1, Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ N lies in only finitely many N_il. For such y that are also good in the sense of step 9, put k(y) := Σ_{(i,l): y∈N_il} ε_il(y)·g_il(y) ∈ ℤ; then Σ_{i,l} 1_{N_il}(y)·g_il(y)·η_il(y) = k(y)·η(y) and |k(y)| ≤ Σ_{i,l} |g_il(y)|·1_{N_il}(y). k agrees Hⁿ-a.e. on N with a Borel ℤ-valued function k̃ (the limit of the Borel partial sums where it exists, 0 elsewhere). The partial sums of Σ_{i,l} 1_{N_il} g_il ⟨ω, η_il⟩ are dominated by |ω|_{E,∞}·Σ_{i,l} |g_il| 1_{N_il}, which is integrable, so by dominated convergence, for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U),
 Q(ω) = ∫_N Σ_{i,l} 1_{N_il}·g_il·⟨ω, η_il⟩ dHⁿ = ∫_N k̃(y)·⟨ω(y), η(y)⟩ dHⁿ(y).

11. The integer multiplicity triple (parent 6(f)–(g); Simon 3.9). Let N₀ ⊆ N be a Borel Hⁿ-null set off which the conclusions of steps 9–10 hold and k = k̃ (Hⁿ is Borel regular). Put N' := {y ∈ N ∖ N₀ : k̃(y) ≠ 0}, θ'(y) := |k̃(y)| for y ∈ N' and θ'(y) := 0 otherwise (ℕ-valued, Borel), and ξ'(y) := sign(k̃(y))·η(y) for y ∈ N' and ξ'(y) := 0 otherwise (Borel). Then R' := (N', θ', ξ') is an IMRep in U:
 – N' is Borel and N' ⊆ N ⊆ U;
 – N' is countably n-rectifiable: N' ⊆ ⋃_i H_i(ℝⁿ) with every H_i Lipschitz on ℝⁿ (the definition of CountablyRectifiable with the null set ∅);
 – θ' is measurable and θ'(y) ≥ 1 for y ∈ N';
 – for every compact C ⊆ U, ∫⁻_{N'∩C} θ' dHⁿ ≤ ∫⁻_N Σ_{i,l} |g_il|·1_{N_il} dHⁿ < ∞;
 – ξ' is Borel, hence a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞N';
 – orientation: by (TL) with (U, A, B) := (ℝ^P, N', N) (N' ⊆ N Borel, Hⁿ(N) < ∞), for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ N' the set N' has the approximate tangent space T_yN at y, and ξ'(y) = ±η(y) is a unit orientation of T_yN by step 9 and (A1).
Finally, for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U): R'.action ω = ∫_{N'} θ'(y)·ξ'(y)(ω(y)) dHⁿ(y) = ∫_{N'} k̃(y)·⟨ω(y), η(y)⟩ dHⁿ(y) = ∫_N k̃·⟨ω, η⟩ dHⁿ = Q(ω), because θ'ξ' = k̃η on N', k̃ = 0 on N ∖ (N' ∪ N₀) and Hⁿ(N₀) = 0 (step 10). So R' represents Q, and Q is integer multiplicity. ∎
proof_key_steps: Restrict to M₁ = M ∩ K (Hⁿ(M₁) < ∞) and replace f by a globally Lipschitz C¹ map f̂ equal to f near K; (TL) and R.orients give oriented approximate tangent planes Hⁿ-a.e. on M₁.
Parametrize M₁ up to a null set by disjoint bi-Lipschitz pieces G_i(A_i) (Rademacher, critical-set area formula, partition into approximately linear pieces, Lusin–Souslin).
Lemma T: at density and Lebesgue points the blow-ups of G(A) converge to DG(u)(ℝⁿ); with (TL) and the Gram–Schmidt algebra, ξ(G_i(u)) = ±DG_i(u)_#e/J_{G_i}(u) (Simon 3.4–3.5).
With H_i = f̂∘G_i and the area formula, Q(ω) = Σ_{i,l} ∫_{N_il} g_il⟨ω, η_il⟩ dHⁿ over bi-Lipschitz image pieces N_il = H_i(A_il), with Σ∫|g_il| ≤ Λⁿ∫_{M₁}θ (Simon 3.6).
Lemma T and (TL) give one orientation η of T_yN with η_il(y) = ±η(y); so Q(ω) = ∫_N k⟨ω, η⟩ with k integer valued, and (N′, |k|, sign(k)η) on {k ≠ 0} is an IMRep representing Q (Simon 3.7–3.9).

subproblems.title: Integer multiplicity calculus: tangent locality, restriction, differences, orientation bound (reuse of the accepted declaration cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub)
subproblems.statement: (a) Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open and M ⊆ M' ⊆ U Borel sets with Hⁿ(M' ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U (Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M and every linear subspace Q, M has approximate tangent space Q at x (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q, Simon Ch. 3, 1.4) if and only if M' does. (b) If U ⊆ ℝ^P is open, R = (M, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in U (contract structure) and E is Borel, then (M ∩ E, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in U and it represents some current in 𝒟_n(U). (c) If U is open and A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U) are integer multiplicity (contract IsIntegerMultiplicity), then so is A − B. (d) For every IMRep R in any U, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ R.carrier, |R.orient(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every n-covector α (|·| the Euclidean coefficient norm).

subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse: this is the comparator-accepted DAG declaration cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub (node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.im_calculus-a1, accepted candidate commit 2af75d6), whose frozen Lean type is reused verbatim; no new formal work is needed. It is the parent's resolved dependency im_calculus, re-listed because the parent uses part (c) in step 3(a) (Y₁ − Y₂ is integer multiplicity) and part (a), with the two sides of ↔ exchanged, to supply the hypothesis (TL) of the sibling pf_integer (step 6(d) of the parent proof: approximate tangent spaces of subsets agree a.e.). Its audited proof is reproduced below; in that text, "the parent proof" and "sibling" refer to the decomposition of root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1, in which it was proved, not to the present node.
Source: Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2) and the density argument in the proof of Theorem 1.6 “⇒” (chapter-03.txt lines 107–160); Ch. 6, Remarks 3.2(1) and 2.9 (chapter-06.txt lines 287–293, 755–768), stated in the book without proof; and Ch. 6, Remark 2.6 for the orientation bound. Hⁿ := μHE[n] throughout. For x ∈ ℝ^P and r > 0, η_{x,r}(y) := r⁻¹(y − x) (SimonGMT blowUpMap). The statement has four parts: (a) locality of approximate tangent spaces, (b) restriction of a representation to a Borel set, (c) differences of integer multiplicity currents, (d) the orientation bound |⟨α, ξ⟩| ≤ |α|; U is open in (a)–(c).

Preliminaries.
(P0) Normalization: SimonGMT's density theorems are stated for simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal n, which equals μHE[n] for natural n (SimonGMT Chapter02 simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_euclideanHausdorffMeasure, with simonHausdorffMeasureReal_toOuterMeasure); hence null sets, finiteness and densities transfer verbatim, and Hⁿ is Borel regular (every set has a Borel hull of the same measure).
(P1) Scaling: for every set A, Hⁿ(η_{x,r}(A)) = r^{−n}Hⁿ(A) (Mathlib Measure.hausdorffMeasure_smul₀ and invariance of Hausdorff measure under isometries). Hence for Borel A and bounded Borel f, ∫_{η_{x,r}(A)} f dHⁿ = r^{−n}∫_A f(η_{x,r}(y)) dHⁿ(y).
(P2) Density zero (SimonGMT Chapter01 simon_theorem_3_6, for the Borel regular outer measure Hⁿ, cf. simon_remark_3_7_hausdorff): if D is Borel with Hⁿ(D) < ∞, then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∉ D, lim_{r↓0} Hⁿ(D ∩ B̄_r(x))/(ω_n rⁿ) = 0.
(P3) Cauchy–Binet. For n×P matrices A, B, det(ABᵀ) = Σ_I det(A_I) det(B_I), the sum over increasing I = (i_1 < ⋯ < i_n) in {1, …, P}, A_I the n×n submatrix of columns I. Proof: the j-th column of ABᵀ is Σ_k B_{jk}A_{·k}, so by multilinearity det(ABᵀ) = Σ_{k_1,…,k_n} B_{1k_1}⋯B_{nk_n} det(A_{·k_1}, …, A_{·k_n}); terms with a repeated index vanish, and grouping the remaining tuples by their underlying increasing tuple I (k = I ∘ σ for a permutation σ) gives Σ_I det(A_I) Σ_σ sgn(σ) Π_j B_{j, I_{σ(j)}} = Σ_I det(A_I)det(B_I). (For n > P both sides are 0 — no increasing I, and rank ABᵀ < n.)
(P4) Orientation bound. If τ_1, …, τ_n are orthonormal in ℝ^P and ⟨α, ζ⟩ = ±α(τ_1, …, τ_n) for all n-covectors α, then |⟨α, ζ⟩| ≤ |α| (Euclidean coefficient norm covectorEuclideanNorm). Proof: with A_{ik} := ⟨τ_i, e_k⟩, multilinearity and the alternating property give α(τ) = Σ_I det(A_I) α(e_I); by Cauchy–Schwarz and (P3), |α(τ)| ≤ |α|(Σ_I det(A_I)²)^{1/2} = |α| det(AAᵀ)^{1/2} = |α|, since AAᵀ = (⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩) is the identity. For n = 0, |α(∅)| = |α|.
(P5) Two unit orientations of the same n-dimensional subspace Q differ by a sign: if τ, τ' are orthonormal bases of Q, τ'_i = Σ_j O_{ij}τ_j with O orthogonal, and α(τ') = det(O)α(τ) = ±α(τ) for every alternating α. Hence IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q and IsUnitOrientationOf ζ' Q imply ζ' = ζ or ζ' = −ζ, and IsUnitOrientationOf (−ζ) Q holds whenever IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q.
(P6) If R = (M, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in an open U, then Hⁿ(M ∩ K) ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U (θ ≥ 1 on M).

(d) Orientation bound. By the orientation field of an IMRep, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ R.carrier there is Q with IsUnitOrientationOf (R.orient x) Q, i.e. an orthonormal τ with ⟨α, R.orient x⟩ = ±α(τ) for all α; by (P4), |R.orient x α| ≤ |α| for all α. (No openness of U is needed.)

(a) Locality. Let U be open, M ⊆ M' ⊆ U Borel with Hⁿ(M' ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, and D := M' ∖ M.
1. For R ∈ ℕ let U_R := {x ∈ U : |x| < R, infDist(x, ℝ^P ∖ U) > 1/R} (U_R := {|x| < R} if U = ℝ^P). U_R is open, closure(U_R) is a compact subset of U, and U_R ↑ U. D_R := D ∩ U_R is Borel with Hⁿ(D_R) ≤ Hⁿ(M' ∩ closure(U_R)) < ∞. By (P2) there is an Hⁿ-null set Z_R such that every x ∉ D_R ∪ Z_R satisfies Hⁿ(D_R ∩ B̄_r(x)) = o(rⁿ) as r ↓ 0. Let Z := ⋃_R Z_R, and let Z' ⊇ Z be a Borel Hⁿ-null set (P0). Let x ∈ M ∖ Z'; choose R with x ∈ U_R and r₀ > 0 with B̄_{r₀}(x) ⊆ U_R. Then x ∉ D_R (as x ∈ M) and D ∩ B̄_r(x) = D_R ∩ B̄_r(x) for r < r₀, so Hⁿ(D ∩ B̄_r(x)) = o(rⁿ).
2. Fix such x, a subspace Q and f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with spt f ⊆ B_ρ(0). For r < r₀/ρ the sets η_{x,r}(M), η_{x,r}(M') meet B_ρ(0) in sets of finite Hⁿ-measure, so the integrals below are genuine Bochner integrals. Since η_{x,r} is injective, η_{x,r}(M') is the disjoint union of η_{x,r}(M) and η_{x,r}(D), and by (P1)
 |∫_{η_{x,r}(M')} f dHⁿ − ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dHⁿ| = |∫_{η_{x,r}(D)} f dHⁿ| ≤ |f|_∞ r^{−n} Hⁿ(D ∩ B_{rρ}(x)) → 0 as r ↓ 0.
Hence for every f the two families of integrals have the same limit as r → 0⁺ or both have none; the condition finrank Q = n is common to both predicates. So HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' x Q for every x ∈ M ∖ Z' and every Q; the exceptional set M ∩ Z' is null for Hⁿ⌞M. ∎

(b) Restriction. Let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an IMRep in the open set U and E a Borel set. Define R' with carrier M ∩ E and the same mult θ and orient ξ.
1. Structure fields: M ∩ E is Borel and contained in U; countably n-rectifiable (CountablyRectifiable.mono); θ is measurable and θ > 0 on M ∩ E; ∫_{M∩E∩K} θ dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U; ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ E) ≤ Hⁿ⌞M.
2. Orientation: by (P6) and (a) applied to M ∩ E ⊆ M ⊆ U, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ E and all Q, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (M ∩ E) x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q. With the orientation field of R (Hⁿ-a.e. on M) this gives the orientation field of R'.
3. The current: A(ω) := ∫_{M∩E} θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). By (d), |θ⟨ω, ξ⟩| ≤ |ω|_∞ θ 1_{tsupport ω} Hⁿ-a.e. on M, and tsupport ω is a compact subset of U, so the integrand is integrable; A is linear. If ω_j → 0 in 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOnConverges: supports in a fixed compact K ⊆ U and uniform convergence of all derivatives, in particular |ω_j|_∞ → 0 since all norms on the finite-dimensional space of n-covectors are equivalent), then |A(ω_j)| ≤ |ω_j|_∞ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ → 0. So A is a GeometricCurrentOn U n and R' represents A (IMRep.Represents, IMRep.action). ∎

(c) Differences. Let A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U), U open, be represented by R_A = (M_A, θ_A, ξ_A) and R_B = (M_B, θ_B, ξ_B).
1. (Borel versions and good points.) Choose Borel ξ̃_A, ξ̃_B equal to ξ_A, ξ_B Hⁿ-a.e. on M_A, resp. M_B (a.e. strong measurability; set them 0 off the carriers). Let G be the set of x ∈ M_A ∪ M_B such that: if x ∈ M_A, then ξ̃_A(x) = ξ_A(x) and there is Q_A(x) with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M_A x Q_A(x) and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ_A x) Q_A(x); the analogous condition for B if x ∈ M_B; and, for each pair (N, N') among (M_A ∩ M_B, M_A), (M_A ∩ M_B, M_B) with x ∈ N, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N' x Q for every Q. By the orientation fields of R_A, R_B, by (P6) and by (a), (M_A ∪ M_B) ∖ G is Hⁿ-null; let N₀ ⊇ (M_A ∪ M_B) ∖ G be a Borel Hⁿ-null set (P0).
2. (Overlap.) Let x ∈ (M_A ∩ M_B) ∖ N₀. The approximate tangent space of M_A ∩ M_B at x exists and equals Q_A(x) and also Q_B(x) (the equivalences defining G and uniqueness of approximate tangent spaces, SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique); so Q_A(x) = Q_B(x) and by (P5) ξ̃_B(x) = ε(x)ξ̃_A(x) with ε(x) ∈ {1, −1}. Put ε(x) := 1 if ξ̃_B(x) = ξ̃_A(x) and ε(x) := −1 otherwise (a Borel function).

6. (Orientation.) For compact K ⊆ U, Hⁿ(M ∩ K) ≤ Hⁿ(M_A ∩ K) + Hⁿ(M_B ∩ K) < ∞ by (P6) applied to R_A, R_B. Apply (a) to the pairs (M ∩ M_A ⊆ M_A), (M ∩ M_A ⊆ M), (M ∩ M_B ⊆ M_B), (M ∩ M_B ⊆ M) (all Borel, contained in U, with locally finite Hⁿ-measure): for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ M_A the approximate tangent spaces of M and of M_A at x coincide (both equal that of M ∩ M_A), and similarly for M_B. subproblems.title: A current vanishing on forms supported away from a compact set has compact support inside it (reuse of the accepted declaration rsd_cmr_support_subset_of_vanish)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, K ⊆ U compact, and F ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with F(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) whose topological support is disjoint from K. Then spt F ⊆ K and spt F is compact. Here spt F = U ∖ Z(F) (GeometricCurrentOn.support), Z(F) being the union of all open W with closure(W) compact, closure(W) ⊆ U and F(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U K : Set (Euclid P)) (F : GeometricCurrentOn U n), IsOpen U → IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) K → F ω = 0) → F.support ⊆ K ∧ IsCompact F.support

It is the parent's resolved dependency support_of_vanishing, re-listed because the parent uses it in step 3(a) (spt(Y₁ − Y₂) is compact and contained in spt Y₁ ∪ spt Y₂) and in step 4 (spt push Y ⊆ f(spt Y), with U = ℝ^P and the compact set f(spt Y)). Its audited proof is reproduced below; in that text, "the parent proof" and "sibling" refer to the decomposition of root.regular_set_dense-a1.constant_multiplicity_reduction-a1, in which it was proved, not to the present node.
Source: parent proof, step 6(f) (“For y ∈ U ∖ K choose s > 0 with B̄_s(y) ⊆ U ∖ K … S − T vanishes on all forms supported in B_{s/2}(y), whose closure is compact and contained in U, so y ∉ spt(S − T). Thus spt(S − T) ⊆ K. Being relatively closed in U and contained in the compact K ⊆ U, spt(S − T) is compact”), isolated for an arbitrary current F; the parent applies it to F = S − T.

1. Points of U ∖ K are not in spt F. Let y ∈ U ∖ K. Since U is open and K is closed (compact), U ∖ K is open (IsOpen.sdiff), so there is s > 0 with B_s(y) ⊆ U ∖ K. Put W := B_{s/2}(y).
 (a) W is open and y ∈ W.
 (b) closure(W) ⊆ B̄_{s/2}(y) ⊆ B_s(y) ⊆ U ∖ K ⊆ U.
 (c) closure(W) is compact, as a closed subset of the compact closed ball B̄_{s/2}(y) (ℝ^P is proper).
 (d) If ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) and tsupport ω ⊆ W, then tsupport ω ⊆ B_s(y) ⊆ U ∖ K is disjoint from K, so F(ω) = 0.
 By (a)-(d), W is one of the sets whose union is Z(F), so y ∈ Z(F) and y ∉ spt F.

2. spt F ⊆ K. By definition spt F ⊆ U, and by step 1 no point of U ∖ K lies in spt F.

3. Compactness. From spt F = U ∖ Z(F), spt F ⊆ K and K ⊆ U, we get spt F = K ∖ Z(F). Z(F) is open, as a union of open sets (isOpen_zeroRegion). So K ∖ Z(F) is a closed subset of the compact set K, hence compact (IsCompact.diff). ∎
proof_key_steps: For y ∈ U ∖ K, a ball B_{s/2}(y) with closure in U ∖ K is a relatively compact zero set of F, so y ∉ spt F.
Hence spt F ⊆ K, and spt F = K ∖ Z(F) is compact because Z(F) is open.
